title: Heartbeat-driven session reconciliation to reduce silent SSE disconnects
creator: Daniel Chu
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers reported unexplained 'silent' Stream (SSE) disconnects during long-lived Hosted API sessions that result in partial outputs and caller-facing timeouts. Investigation indicates a confluence of factors: idle timeouts in upstream load balancers, ephemeral TCP resets from intermediate NATs, and gaps where the server did not emit explicit progress heartbeats for long generation tails. This ticket implements a server-driven heartbeat and lightweight session reconciliation protocol to reduce these silent disconnects and provide deterministic partial-output recovery.
problem_statement: Hosted SSE connections occasionally drop without a final close or error event. Clients are left waiting and frequently surface partial outputs as failures. This is causing repeated customer escalations and degradation of SLAs for large-output streaming workloads.
root_cause_summary:
- No regular liveliness events during long token generation tails; upstream network appliances prune idle TCP flows.
- Existing resume/patch mechanisms assume explicit disconnect events and sequence metadata; when TCP resets happen silently, the session is orphaned.
- Some client SDK versions don't aggressively reconnect or provide session checkpoints, increasing end-to-end time-to-recovery.
proposed_solution:
1) Emit small heartbeat 'probe' SSE events (type: "heartbeat_probe") every 25s during active streams when no token events have been emitted for >=20s.
2) Add server-side lightweight session checkpoints anchored at chunk boundaries: checkpoint contains session_id, last_sequence_id, model_variant, and opaque resume_token.
3) Implement reconcile endpoint /v1/streams/reconcile that accepts resume_token and returns any missing suffix chunks or an instruction to fallback to model-variant-stream fallback.
4) Client SDK patch (minor): attempt transparent reconnect on heartbeat timeout with exponential backoff and automatic POST to reconcile endpoint to fetch missing tokens to append to local buffer.
5) Feature flag rollout and metric gating (enabled=false by default for initial deploy).
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Additional heartbeat traffic increases per-connection byte rate (negligible compared to tokens but measurable under millions of concurrent streams).
- Checkpoints add small state retention per session (TTL=2 minutes by default); needs memory accounting in the serving runtime.
- Reconciliation path may cause duplicate tokens if client already received tail; tokens are idempotent based on sequence ids to dedupe.
- Some legacy clients not on the SDK will not benefit until they implement the reconcile flow; provide clear HTTP fallback semantics.
- Rolling out heartbeats may mask upstream infra issues; we will still add LB config guidance to customers and require load balancer idle timeout >= 60s where possible.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Dev): server heartbeat emission + checkpoint persistence (local in-memory with shared cache fallback), reconcile endpoint, and unit tests.
Phase 2 (Canary): enable feature flag for 5% of hosted traffic; deploy client SDK patch to internal customers and Redwood integration tests.
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout): monitor session-reset-rate, stream-completion-rate, and customer error reports; expand to 25% then 100%.
Phase 4: provide runbook and config suggestions for Dedicated/Private customers and backport minimal server-only heartbeat to runtime-1.20 LTS.
metrics_and_alerting:
New and updated metrics:
- sse.heartbeat.sent (counter)
- sse.heartbeat.missed (counter)
- sse.session.reconciliations (counter)
- sse.session.reset_rate (gauge)
- sse.partial-output-incidents (counter, pipeline-derived)
Alerting thresholds: session_reset_rate > 0.5% sustained 10m for tenant with >1000 streams => P1 pager.
Dashboards: add per-tenant breakdown and 95th tail for time-to-recover metrics.
rollout_and_monitoring:
- Deploy behind feature flag off.
- Enable for subset of internal customers and test harness first.
- After 48 hours with no regression signals, open Canary to 5%.
- Observe reconcilations and missed heartbeat trends; if recon rate > 0.2% for a stable shard, pause and investigate.
- Backfill: if reconcile returns chunks, server will record reconciliation latency and number of tokens backfilled; emit telemetry for SRE review.
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for heartbeat emission logic and TTL expiration.
- Integration tests: simulate upstream idle timeouts and NAT resets; assert client SDK reconnect + /reconcile returns correct suffix.
- Load test: run 100k concurrent synthetic long-tail streams with heartbeats enabled to validate CPU/heap overhead.
- Compatibility tests: older SDK clients should receive explicit SSE 'session-stale' event and return HTTP 409 from reconcile endpoint with recommended client-side steps.
risks:
- Memory overhead in high-concurrency hosts if checkpoints retained too long. Mitigation: default TTL=120s, max checkpoints per host cap with LRU eviction.
- Possible duplicate delivery surface for clients not deduping by seq id. Mitigation: include sequence and opaque resume token and document idempotency semantics.
- Unexpected load on reconcile endpoint during a global network event. Mitigation: rate limit per-tenant and add exponential backoff guidance, plus fallback to non-streaming generation endpoint.
next_steps: Publish SDK patch for Node and Python (links in attachments) and coordinate with DS for QA
Schedule canary on infra-candidate bucket and notify SRE on-call
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket opened after customer call that reproduced silent disconnect on a 6-minute generation. Initial triage assigned to Lena.
2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by injecting FIN on idle TCP after 30s in our test harness. Root cause narrowed to lack of liveliness events when generator stalls between tokens.
2026-03-12: Rapid prototype implemented: server emits minimal heartbeat SSE comment (':hb') every 25s. Confirmed upstream LB (Envoy) keeps flow alive when heartbeat present.
2026-03-13: Checkpoint format sketched; reconciler endpoint contract reviewed with API team. Draft PR created for server work (see attachments).
2026-03-14: Load test in staging with 50k concurrent streams shows ~0.7% memory increase and acceptable CPU tail. Proceed to canary gating; feature flag default=false.
